comments.author: miXXed
comments.body_html:
Thanks for the bug report! You were spot on. It was indeed a conflict with “Lots of Loot”.

What happened: The config contained some IDs that “Lots of Loot” couldn’t handle, causing the server to crash during raid loading and signing you out.

The fix: I’ve removed all problematic IDs from the config. The mod now works flawlessly alongside “Lots of Loot”!

Update v1.0.1 will be released shortly with the fix.

Thanks for your patience and for helping me identify this issue! If you encounter any other problems, feel free to let me know.

comments.author: firstname lastName
comments.body_html: As a KIL user this is interesting. The description says KeyHunter doesn’t affect loot balance but what does that mean? For example If we set a value of 999999 would a duffel bag be full of 12 random keys? I felt like high values in KIL replaced whatever loot could have been inside a jacket/duffel/dead scav.

comments.author: miXXed
comments.body_html:
Good question, and that’s a valid concern.

KeyHunter does not remove or replace any existing vanilla loot entries. It only adds keys to the loot pool of the selected containers using Tarkov’s relative probability system.

However, very high values will strongly skew the loot roll in favor of keys. In that case, keys can dominate the container’s rolls and effectively crowd out other items, which can feel like the original loot was replaced.

So it’s not a hard replacement done by the mod, but a result of how Tarkov’s loot weighting works. This is why the default value is kept much lower and meant to be adjusted gradually.

Hey, thanks for the feedback! A few things to check:

  1. What’s your baseKeySpawnChance set to in config.json? The default is 500 - higher values will make keys more dominant in containers.
  2. Are you running any other loot mods (like LotsOfLoot)? They can multiply the effect.

If you can share your config.json and your full mod list, I can help narrow it down. Maybe in private chat?
